clue.text: Discovered paper became a bit brown

parts.note: to be discovered doing something is to be caught at it
The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone was found out, and the newspaper ended up slightly browned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' reads as a description of the paper, but it is CAUGHT, and 'paper' is THE SUN, a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch the sun is the idiom for getting slightly tanned or sunburnt outdoors.

clue.text: After a couple of pages double up and clap

indicators.note: the clue's opening word sets the order: the pages come first and the reversed piece follows them

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for page, so two pages is PP

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from the bottom upwards, turning it round

parts.note: dual means double, twofold

explanation.surface: Someone stuck on page two folds over laughing and applauds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' only works in a down clue, where the reversed word reads upwards; 'After' sets the order rather than signalling a deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: To applaud is to show approval by clapping the hands.

clue.text: Most tender man in case

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a man
lest means for fear that, in case

explanation.surface: The kindest man in a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentlest is the superlative of gentle, mild and soft-hearted, so the most tender.

clue.text: Second alcoholic rises to throw up!

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from the bottom up, turning the whole run round

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard

explanation.surface: Another drunk gets to his feet and vomits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns S + SOT round, so SSOT reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To toss is to throw upwards, as with a coin or a pancake.

clue.text: Blow dismissal, retire!

parts.note: a hit is a blow or strike
getting the sack is being dismissed from a job

explanation.surface: A setback: fired from work, so time to give up and quit.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitting the sack is an idiom for going to bed, retiring for the night.

clue.text: Teetotal, thus an alcoholic drink is pointless

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

indicators.note: without a point, here a compass point: the letter for east is taken away

parts.note: beer is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone abstaining says a boozy drink is a waste of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' removes E (east, a compass point) from BEER to leave BER.
explanation.definitionFit: Teetotal and sober both describe someone not drinking alcohol, abstinent.

clue.text: Having vehicle in rain could be heaven?

indicators.note: the vehicle word is placed inside the rearranged letters
the letters of rain could be arranged another way

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: With a van parked out in the rain, someone wonders if this is paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges the rain letters as NIRA; 'Having' is a link. The question mark flags that heaven is a loose sense of a Buddhist term.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana is the Buddhist state of perfect bliss, loosely used for paradise, hence the question mark.

clue.text: They stand on street corners stopping motorists

definitions.text: They stand on street corners stopping motorists

parts.words: They stand on street corners stopping motorists
parts.note: suggests people loitering on corners flagging drivers down, but describes the signals at junctions that halt cars on red

explanation.definitionFit: Signals at road junctions show red to halt drivers, standing on corners as posts.

clue.text: Used to give motorist directions?

parts.note: suggests something like a map or sat nav, but it is what the motorist uses to steer the car in a chosen direction

explanation.definitionFit: The driver turns this wheel to point the car where it should go.

clue.text: Sent out after material, is sorry

indicators.note: the rearranged word comes after the material in the answer

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of sent are disordered

explanation.surface: A fabric sent out comes with an apology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the sent letters to ENTS. Rep is a ribbed cloth for upholstery and ties, a word mostly met in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Repenting is feeling remorse for a wrong, being sorry for it.

clue.text: Flap tore, ruining seat

parts.note: a tab is a small flap

indicators.note: ruining signals that the letters of tore are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: A flap ripped, spoiling a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruining' rearranges the tore letters to ORET. A taboret is a low upholstered stool, a word rarer than its parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A taboret is a low stool, a kind of seat without arms or back.

clue.text: Feeble female bird

parts.note: a rail is a wading marsh bird

explanation.surface: A weak hen.
explanation.definitionFit: Frail and feeble are synonyms for weak and delicate.

clue.text: Brief years of famine

parts.note: short means brief
an age is a long span of years

explanation.surface: A short spell of famine years.
explanation.definitionFit: A famine is a severe lack, especially of food, so a scarcity.

clue.text: Student, taking one guy in, cheated and copied

indicators.note: the student, one and guy go inside the word for cheated

parts.note: duped means tricked, cheated
L, the learner plate, stands for a student
I is the Roman numeral one
cat is slang for a man, a guy

explanation.surface: A student brought in a fellow, cheated and copied his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat' as slang for a man comes from jazz talk; 'taking' is a link, and 'in' sends all three pieces into the word for cheated.
explanation.definitionFit: Duplicated means reproduced exactly, made a copy of.

clue.text: One US design I developed under cover

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: developed signals the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: An American design project goes under wraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' is the anagram signal, as a photo or a plan is developed, and 'One' gives the Roman numeral at the front. 'under cover' reads like secret agents, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In disguise means concealed, hidden, as if undercover.

clue.text: Duty on current vehicle

parts.note: a tax is a duty levied
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: A levy on the current car.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a hired car, a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Product perished before closing date

indicators.note: the word for perished comes before the product word

parts.note: dead means perished
a line is a range of products a firm sells

explanation.surface: A product went off before its sell-by date.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadline is the last date by which something must be done, a cut-off.

clue.text: Woman following boy said why

indicators.note: the sound-alike letter follows the boy word

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: said signals that the word why is heard as a letter

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like Y

explanation.surface: A woman trailing a boy asks why.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' turns 'why' into the letter Y, which comes after LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady is a polite word for a woman.

clue.text: Declines to bother including cleaners

indicators.note: the word for declines holds the word for bother inside it

parts.note: dies means declines, fades away
to ail is to trouble or bother

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to trouble the cleaning staff.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'daily' is a cleaner who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily is a British term for a domestic help who comes in every day to clean.

clue.text: Film the Queen in Gateshead, sparkling

parts.note: a flick is a film
ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina
read as Gate's head, the first letter of gate

explanation.surface: A movie shows the Queen visiting Gateshead, a northern English town, glittering.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town in north-east England, but here it is split as 'Gate's head', giving G.
explanation.definitionFit: Flickering light wavers and twinkles, so it is sparkling.

clue.text: "Tail", in a different language

indicators.note: different asks for the letters in another order

explanation.surface: The word 'tail' given in another tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges TAIL, IN and A together.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian is a Romance tongue spoken in Italy.

clue.text: Counselling New Guinea DC

indicators.note: new signals the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Advice for the island nation of New Guinea in Washington DC.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Guinea' looks like the country, but 'New' is the anagram signal for GUINEA and DC.
explanation.definitionFit: Guidance is advice or counselling given to help someone.

clue.text: Plunge tip of knife into unusually lean joint

indicators.note: plunging a blade drives it inside something
into says where the plunged letter goes: inside the rearranged word
unusually signals the letters of lean are set out in an odd order
the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A knife is stabbed into a joint of thin meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip of knife' gives K; 'unusually' rearranges LEAN as ANLE; 'Plunge ... into' puts K inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint between the foot and the leg.

clue.text: Made at Hull in the end?

indicators.note: in tells the solver the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: Something was manufactured in Hull, an English port city, at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points into 'maDE AT Hull'. 'the end' looks like a pointer to final letters, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Death is the end of life, so a fair definition with the question mark.

clue.text: Or turned up, having taken Ken off list?

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom, so the word is written backwards
off means the name is removed from the word before it

explanation.surface: Someone asks if the roster was overturned after Ken was struck from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' makes RO from OR; 'off' takes KEN from TAKEN, leaving TA.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a list of people's turns at a duty, a schedule.

clue.text: Trifle kitten's tumbled right into!

indicators.note: the right letter goes inside the rearranged letters
tumbled signals the letters of kitten fall into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A kitten has fallen headlong into a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tumbled' rearranges KITTEN as TINKET, and 'into' puts R inside it. 'Trifle' looks like the pudding, but it means a small thing of little value.
explanation.definitionFit: A trinket is a small ornament of little worth, a trifle.

clue.text: Hole's round if in cereal packet

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: in places the word if inside the cereal
the cereal packs the small word inside it like a packet

parts.note: rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A hole in a round cereal box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'packet' together signal the container: the cereal wraps round the little word like a box. 'Hole's' gives the definition plus a link 's.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is an opening, a mouth or hole.

clue.text: Uses very little money and is relieved?

definitions.meaning: literally, pays out just one small coin
relieving oneself is going to the toilet

explanation.definitionFit: Literally paying out a single coin; also a British euphemism for urinating, from the old coin-operated public toilet doors.
